name: amazon_search_chromium
description: Amazon search results page. Returns one flat array per field across result cards; consumers zip them by index. ROW-ALIGNMENT INVARIANT: each field must match exactly one node per card, so every field anchors to a per-card container Amazon renders on EVERY card (title-recipe / price-recipe / asin-faceout-container) and digs the value out of that container's html by regex. A container that is present but empty yields null in the correct slot; a selector that matches NOTHING does not yield null — it shrinks the array and silently misaligns every row after it. So never point a field at an element that only exists when the value does (e.g. .a-price .a-offscreen directly): anchor to the always-present container instead. Localizes by domain (.com/.co.uk/.de). block_assets off so lazy product images load. ENGINE: Chromium (Playwright). WebGL identity follows this host — an AMD Radeon 780M claim under a Windows UA — via chromium_webgl_identity(); no fingerprint_profile, which the Chromium runner would accept and ignore. MEASURED 2026-08-27 (n=2 per locale, 6 runs per engine, research/preset_audit_dual_engine_2026_08_27.json): 4/6 runs returned data on BOTH engines — no separation at this sample size, and neither variant is recommended over the other. This one was clean on de and uk (22 rows each) and blocked 2/2 on us (HTTP 503 plus captcha, 3 retries each); the twin reached all three markets but lost one de and one us run to an HTTP 200 whose titles selector matched nothing — consistent with this repo's known Amazon throttle page served as a 200, though the page HTML is deliberately not in the record, so read its zero retries there as possibly an undetected block rather than as health. The whole margin is one successful us run. Both engines shared the preset's defects at that time: urls came back 22/22 relative on every successful run, with 6 sponsored /sspa/click entries mixed into the organic list. FIXED 2026-08-28 (round 0): urljoin resolved organic urls absolute and null_if_regex nulled the sponsored row's url in place -- closing the relative-url defect but only half of the sponsored one, since deleting the url identified a sponsored row without recovering its real destination, and its None was indistinguishable from a drifted selector. FIX ROUND 1 2026-08-28: Amazon's own sponsored redirect carries the real destination inline (`/sspa/click?...&url=%2Freal%2Fpath`), so `urls` now UNWRAPS it via a new `unwrap_param` op (percent-decodes the `url` query parameter; passes any other value through unchanged, which is what lets one pipeline handle organic and sponsored hrefs together) and then resolves it absolute the same way as every organic url -- every row gets a real, followable destination, sponsored included. A parallel `sponsored` field (same selector, same length) carries a non-null marker exactly on the rows that were unwrapped, so a caller can still filter organic-only without losing data. Verified live 2026-08-28 against real amazon.de and amazon.co.uk search pages, and against all 48 real sponsored hrefs recorded in the 2026-08-27 dual-engine audit (research/preset_audit_dual_engine_2026_08_27.json): amazon.de sometimes serves its results under an English-UI /-/en/ path prefix, which lands in front of the sponsored redirect too (/-/en/sspa/click?...) -- unlike round 0's anchored exclusion pattern (which MISSED every sponsored row under this prefix), neither `unwrap_param` (matches `url=` anywhere) nor the `sponsored` marker's regex (matches `sspa/click` anywhere) depend on where in the path the wrapper sits, so this shape needed no special-casing. FIX ROUND 2 2026-08-28: `sponsored` now yields a non-null value on EVERY row (an always-matching alternation: the literal `sspa/click` when present, an empty string otherwise) instead of null on an organic row -- reads as truthy-vs-empty rather than value-vs-null, so a genuinely ad-free page no longer trips a false silent-null warning. FIX ROUND 3 (final review): that alternation now carries `(?s)`. `.` does not cross a newline, so on an href whose wrapper sits after one the `(?!.*sspa/click)` branch could not see the wrapper to refute itself, matched empty at position 0, and reported the row ORGANIC while `unwrap_param` -- whose pattern uses no `.` -- unwrapped it anyway: the two fields disagreeing on the same row, which this description says cannot happen. HTML attribute values may legally contain newlines. Regression-tested in tests/presets/test_amazon_search_row_alignment.py. CORRECTION (measured, not fixed): the marker's own death is still indistinguishable from a healthy ad-free page -- if Amazon renamed sspa/click, every row would read "" (not sponsored), byte-identical to a real ad-free run; only the false alarm was closed, not that gap. `prices`/`ratings` now declare their items as nullable too (measured in the same audit: 5/176 and 15/176 nulls respectively, by design per the row-alignment invariant above) -- this repo's self-heal hands `output_schema` to the LLM as the target contract, so a schema claiming a column can never be null was steering a heal toward exactly the per-row selector shape this preset forbids. MEASURED 2026-08-28 (retest of the same twenty presets through the same harness after the five audit fixes; n=2 per locale, 92 runs, research/preset_audit_dual_engine_2026_08_28.json): 4/6 runs returned data, both losses on us -- unchanged from 08-27, and still an access problem, not a parsing one. THE URL DEFECT IS CLOSED here too: 22/22 absolute urls on every successful run, 0 still wrapped, `sponsored` the same length as `urls` with 6 marked, and 0 disagreements between the marker and the ad marker in the resolved destination over this variant's 88 rows. One improvement worth naming: BOTH us failures fired "Captcha/block detected by heuristic" this round, one of them at HTTP 200 -- the 200-variant throttle page that this repo has previously seen pass as an ordinary selector miss was correctly classified as a block. ratings null 2/88, by design.
